Article Title: 'Incompatible with secular character': Centre tells Delhi HC mosque inside Krishi Bhawan must be demolished
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Tuesday informed the Delhi high court that it is planning to remove a mosque situated within the Krishi Bhawan complex to facilitate the redevelopment and reconstruction of the Common Central Secretariat under the Central Vista project.In a status report filed through the Land and Development Office, the Centre also submitted that Krishi Bhawan and the Central Secretariat complex are secular public premises dedicated exclusively to administrative functions. It said the establishment or retention of a permanent religious structure within a central government office complex would be incompatible with the secular character of government property.The Centre maintained that Qadeemi Masjid stands on government-owned land and that its caretaking committee was granted only permissive possession of the premises under an agreement executed on November 8, 1940.The government also claimed that the agreement did not confer any ownership rights, title or interest in the property upon the managing committee.The agreement contained a provision empowering government authorities to take back possession of the property in the event of any breach or default in complying with its terms and conditions.The Centre has relied on an agreement dated November 8, 1940, executed between the then government, as the owner of the property, and the secretary of the managing committee of Jama Masjid.Under the agreement, the government had granted permissive possession of the premises to the committee exclusively for use as a mosque.The agreement also imposed several restrictions on the use and modification of the property, prohibiting the managing committee from making alterations, undertaking repairs to the existing buildings, constructing graves or raising any new structure, even temporarily, without obtaining prior written approval from the government.Mosque required to be removed for execution of Central Vista projectThe Centre said the removal of the structure was necessary as the Central Vista Redevelopment Master Plan provides for the redevelopment and reconstruction of Common Central Secretariat Buildings 4 and 5 at Plot No. 120, covering the existing sites of Shastri Bhawan and Krishi Bhawan.According to the status report, the proposed project is aimed at modernising infrastructure considered essential for the country's governance and administrative functioning. The government has asserted that the mosque presently stands within the identified project site and is required to be removed for the execution of the proposed construction.Describing the construction of CCS Buildings 4 and 5 as a public project of paramount national importance, the Centre also argued that retaining the mosque or reserving any portion of the project site for the religious structure would be inconsistent with the redevelopment master plan.The L&DO has further argued that public land situated in a central administrative zone cannot be permanently reserved for a religious structure.Based on these submissions, the Centre has maintained that the managing committee cannot claim a right to compel the government to allot or earmark a separate portion of land for the mosque within the Krishi Bhawan compound or the Central Secretariat complex.The government has also disputed any violation of the fundamental right to freedom of religion guaranteed under Article 25 of the Constitution.It has submitted that the constitutional provision does not confer a right to insist on worship at a particular place on government land held under a permissive arrangement.The government's response comes in reply to a petition filed by Qadeemi Masjid through its caretaking committee, challenging the proposed action concerning the religious structure.The petition further states that the Delhi Waqf Board notified the property as Waqf property in 1970 and recorded its antiquity.The petitioners claimed that even after Krishi Bhawan, Shastri Bhawan and surrounding government offices were constructed in the 1950s and 1960s, the mosque continued to exist and was used by Muslim employees of the offices for offering prayers.The petitioners acknowledged that the land underneath the mosque is government property but expressed apprehension over the ongoing redevelopment, which involves dismantling the existing complex.They maintained that they have no objection to the Central Vista redevelopment project and are not seeking a suspension or delay in the construction of the Common Central Secretariat buildings.
Article Summary: The Centre is planning to remove a mosque situated within the Krishi Bhawan complex to facilitate the redevelopment of the Common Central Secretariat under the Central Vista project. The Centre said the establishment or retention of a permanent religious structure within a central government office complex would be incompatible with the secular character of government property.

Article Title: At Anant Ambani’s Vantara, global zoos turn to shared data to protect wildlife
Article Text: The EARAZA Annual Conference 2026 concluded at Vantara in Jamnagar, bringing together wildlife professionals, veterinarians, scientists and conservation leaders from 98 institutions across 30 countries, along with representatives of 29 Indian zoological institutions.Held under the theme “Strengthening Global Partnerships for Wildlife Conservation”, the four-day conference focused on cross-border conservation programmes, animal welfare, wildlife medicine, technology, crisis response and public engagement.The conference opened on October 26 with a performance by three-time Grammy Award-winning composer and environmentalist Ricky Kej. The inauguration was followed by a traditional lamp-lighting ceremony attended by Vivaan Karani, CEO, Vantara; Svetlana Akulova, president, EARAZA; Prof Raman Sukumar of the Indian Institute of Science; Dr V Clement Ben, member secretary, Central Zoo Authority; and Dr Brij Kishor Gupta, director, Gujarat Zoological Research and Rescue Centre.The Indian Zoo Yearbook, Volume 11, 2026, was also released during the opening ceremony.As host, Vantara announced that the ANTZ Software Platform would be offered free of cost to all EARAZA members for one year. ANTZ is a zoological management platform with an Open Data Exchange that enables participating institutions to share information across the network.The announcement aligned with one of the conference's key themes: the need for conservation knowledge and data to move more easily between institutions and across national borders. Akulova spoke about the importance of creating global data infrastructure for biodiversity conservation, allowing information generated by one institution to inform decisions elsewhere.The sessions covered coordinated conservation programmes for the Amur tiger, Oriental stork, Blakiston’s eagle-owl and great bustard. Discussions also examined the conservation breeding of Boiga snakes, the reintroduction of the long-eared hedgehog, the conservation of the Indian wild ass and the ex-situ conservation of the Amur tiger.The second day focused on coexistence, urban biodiversity and public engagement. Sessions examined snake conservation and snakebite prevention, biodiversity conservation in million-plus cities and the role of citizen science.A panel on “Animal Welfare: From Inputs to Measurable Outcomes”, moderated by Karani, discussed how care practices can be assessed through measurable outcomes for individual animals. Other sessions addressed the visitor experience at zoological institutions, conservation education and the role of mass media. Wildlife biologist and television presenter Forrest Galante spoke about taking conservation conversations to wider audiences.Delegates also discussed crisis management in wildlife-care facilities and disaster response in the wild. Presentations covered polar bear rescue, wildlife disease diagnostics, animal nutrition and the work of zoological institutions in Russia. Padma Shri awardee Dr K K Sarma, known for his work with elephants, shared field perspectives on human-wildlife conflict.The conference also included interactive formats such as “The Elephant in the Room”, where delegates reflected on difficult questions facing the zoological sector, and the Solution Station, which invited professionals to bring real challenges in wildlife care and conservation for expert guidance.Technology and research took centre stage on the third day. Vantara presented tools developed under the ANTZ platform, including Vespr, an edge-AI bioacoustic monitor that identifies species on the device; Smart Egg Analysis, which helps teams measure and monitor eggs; and an NFC-enabled system for digitally recording animal-care rounds.Scientific presentations by Vantara experts covered non-invasive population genomics of Asiatic lions, paraveterinary training, avian rewilding, the use of artificial intelligence to understand animals and efforts to bridge ex-situ and in-situ conservation.Alongside the sessions, the conference featured an exhibition with 13 exhibitors from seven countries. The displays included veterinary technologies, wildlife diagnostics, genomics, automated microscopy, assisted reproduction systems, avian incubation equipment and remote drug-delivery solutions. Vantara’s host pavilions also featured innovations in wildlife care, nutrition, architecture and technology, along with a virtual reality experience.The final day focused on science-based care for rescued Asian elephants, animal nutrition in rescue and rewilding, habitat change, cryopreservation, triage and parasite surveillance. Dr Manilal Valliyate, chief communication officer at Vantara, moderated a panel on veterinary capacity-building.The conference concluded with a gala dinner and closing ceremony, where Lifetime Achievement Awards were presented to six leaders from India and abroad: Svetlana Akulova, René Franěk, Azer Huseynov, S C Sharma, Dr D N Singh and Dr B S Bonal.The EARAZA flag was then handed over to China, host of the 2027 conference. The event concluded with a vote of thanks by Dr Brij Kishor Gupta.
Article Summary: The EARAZA Annual Conference 2026 concluded at Vantara in Jamnagar, India. It brought together wildlife professionals, veterinarians, scientists and conservation leaders from 98 institutions across 30 countries. The four-day conference focused on cross-border conservation programmes, animal welfare, wildlife medicine, technology, crisis response and public engagement.

Article Title: Row erupts after Scottish govt sends IT contract to Bengaluru to administer welfare payment
Article Text:
Scotland’s SNP government faces criticism for awarding a £35.4 million contract to Bengaluru-based Mphasis to manage its welfare benefits platform, which serves around two million citizens

TOI correspondent from London:

The Scottish National Party, which governs Scotland, has come under fire from opposition ministers for handing a £35.4 million (almost Rs 450 crore) contract to an IT services company in Bengaluru.Under the contract, Mphasis will manage and maintain Scotland’s benefits management platform that delivers welfare benefits to around two million citizens across Scotland.Scotland first minister John Swinney has just returned from a trade mission to India where he was meant to be finding opportunities to support jobs and prosperity across Scotland, so news that he has instead sent lucrative work to India has sparked fiery criticism back home.Scottish Labour’s social justice spokesman, Mark Griffin, told the “Scottish Mail on Sunday”: “We should be using public contracts like this to boost local business and the Scottish economy and create jobs in Scotland. All too often, under SNP, good work has flowed overseas. SNP ministers should explain why this decision was made.”Shadow secretary of state for Scotland Harriet Cross posted on X: “They send millions to India to help administer their ballooning benefits system.This is taxpayers’ money. And they’re sending it abroad.”“Our ongoing relationship with Social Security Scotland allows us to support one of the country’s most critical public service platforms, and our commitment is to maintain continuity, improve operational efficiency and deliver meaningful outcomes for individuals and families across Scotland. The project aligns with our broader public sector focus; supporting govt organisations in running secure, reliable and future-ready digital services,” said Ashish Devalekar, executive vice-president and head of Europe, Mphasis.A Social Security Scotland spokesperson told TOI: “Contracts are awarded in line with the Scottish govt’s procurement guidelines, which state that bids are to be treated equally, regardless of the location. This ensures that we award contracts to the bidder offering the best overall value. Investment in technology ensures we are future proof and adaptable to changing demands for our payments.”Sources in the Scottish govt told TOI that the platform “requires highly specialised expertise in a niche technology area with a relatively small number of suppliers globally able to demonstrate the scale, experience and capability required”.
Article Summary: Scotland’s SNP government faces criticism for awarding a £35.4 million contract to Bengaluru-based Mphasis. Under the contract, Mphasis will manage and maintain Scotland's benefits management platform that delivers welfare benefits to around two million citizens. Scotland first minister John Swinney has just returned from a trade mission to India.

Article Title: SC orders trial in Ram temple donation case; SIT says Rs 2.7 crore stolen
Article Text:
SC clears trial of eight accused of siphoning Rs 2.7 crore in Ayodhya Ram temple donations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Five months after news broke of pilferage of donations at Ayodhya Ram temple, Supreme Court cleared trial of eight people, who figure in the chargesheet filed by the SIT for allegedly siphoning Rs 2.7 crore. It also gave the petitioners, who had sought probe, the status of victims of crime and allowed them to assist in the trial, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.The SIT's status report informed SC that financial and forensic examination extended to cash deposits, transactions, property purchases, construction expenditure, vehicles, jewellery, other assets, and event-related spendings. "The amount of alleged embezzlement is approximately Rs 2.7 crore," the report said.On Monday, solicitor general Tushar Mehta explained to the court the process that involved scrutiny of bank accounts and acquisition of immoveable properties by the accused, as well as examination of CCTV footage that culminated in the chargesheet Sept 23.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the trial court to proceed with the trial in accordance with law. On the large number of petitioners who had sought an independent probe into the donation theft, the bench said the petitioners can be given the status of victims of crime, and in public interest, they can assist the prosecutor and trial court in proceedings.One of the petitioners also sought a direction from SC for an “independent, impartial, technically competent survey/demarcation” of the land that was allotted for the temple by SC in its Nov 9, 2019, judgement.He also sought a direction to the revenue and statutory authorities to place before SC relevant records and their comparison with the site plan and actual location of the Ram Janmabhoomi Temple complex to determine if the present complex stands on the land allotted by the court.While Mehta said it is impermissible for the petitioner to seek a virtual reopening of the judgement by a fivejudge bench, the bench said if the petitioner had any grievance about the demarcation of the land, he should approach the civil court with a civil suit.
Article Summary: Supreme Court clears trial of eight accused of siphoning Rs 2.7 crore in Ayodhya Ram temple donations. It also gave the petitioners, who had sought probe, the status of victims of crime and allowed them to assist in the trial.

Article Title: SC on Diwali: Crackers on Nov 7-8 in 2 time slots, and keep it green
Article Text:
SC allows green crackers in Delhi-NCR on November 7 and 8 during specified hours

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Holding that Deepawali has a religious, social, psychological and emotional significance for people, Supreme Court on Monday kept the window open for bursting of green firecrackers on Nov 7 and 8 between 6am and 7am, and between 8pm and 10pm.The court had allowed bursting of crackers at the same time last year too.A bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale directed police and administration to ensure polluting crackers remain out of bounds for people in Delhi, and take punitive action against those who deal in such crackers.While acknowledging Deepawali's significance, the court stressed that the right of an individual to engage in a particular practice, which may have a religious colour, was only a qualified one and not exempt from restrictions allowed by the Constitution."...Allowing the environment to degrade, which results in a health hazard to all living beings, defeats the very purpose of the festivities... All parties before us are ad idem (of one mind) on the fact that bursting of firecrackers is contributing enormously to pollution in Delhi/NCR," it said. Restriction on manufacture and sale of crackers in the national capital will continue after Diwali.The bench, however, did not favour a complete ban on firecrackers.“Though imposition of a blanket ban seems to be the ideal solution, we are of the opinion that this court, at this point in time, is short of adequate data to decide whether or not a complete ban would be the best solution to solve the problem of environmental pollution, caused by bursting firecrackers,” it said.The bench directed district collectors/commissioners, in consultation with the superintendent of police concerned, to identify and designate locations in the NCR to facilitate the sale of green crackers and banned online sale. “The sale of firecrackers shall be strictly prohibited in any other location, other than the designated ones, including sale through online platforms,” it said.“We direct the authorities concerned to mandate all manufacturers and traders of firecrackers in Delhi-NCR to furnish a monetary security, which shall be a handsome amount, as determined by them. The said security deposit shall immediately stand forfeited in case any manufacturer or trader of firecrackers violates any of the directions passed by this court,” the bench said.The court noted in its order that bursting of firecrackers, though constituting a religious practice meant to celebrate the occasion, would result in severe environmental pollution, especially air and noise, apart from the creation of solid waste. It said the unregulated practice affected everyone, including the end user and, among human beings, children, disabled and elderly people constituted the most vulnerable groups.“It is not in dispute that the right to practice, profess and propagate religion conferred under Article 25(1) of the Constitution is certainly subject to public order, morality, health and other provisions of Part III of the Constitution. This court has repeatedly held that ‘right to life’ envisaged under Article 21 of the Constitution includes the right to a healthy, safe and pollution-free environment, and the said position has been crystallised and, hence, requires no repetition.Therefore, the right of an individual to engage in a particular practice, which may have a religious colour, is only a qualified one and cannot go beyond constitutional restrictions,” the bench said.It added that there shall be no manufacture or sale of firecrackers joined in series (‘ladis’) and garlands. Use of firecrackers with barium and those not approved by CSIRNEERI as green crackers shall not be permitted.
Article Summary: SC allows green crackers in Delhi-NCR on November 7 and 8 during specified hours. Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale directed police and administration to ensure polluting crackers remain out of bounds. Restriction on manufacture and sale of crackers will continue after Diwali.

Article Title: Cyclone Murasu crosses Andhra coast, gale winds up to 120 kmph - top developments
Article Text:
Here are the top developments:

Storm surge threat in Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam

Andhra govt rolls out grievance reporting mechanism

19 flights cancelled in Andhra Pradesh

Andhra Pradesh on high alert

Tamil Nadu sends NDRF, power teams to Andhra

Odisha evacuates people, puts 300 rescue teams on standby

NEW DELHI: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu made landfall along the south Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole early Tuesday, with its eye entering the coast and a major part of its wall cloud moving over land, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. The landfall point is between Nellore and Narsapur.Gale winds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph, are likely along and off the coast during landfall and are expected to persist. The IMD has also forecast heavy rainfall over the next 12 hours and a storm surge of 1-1.5 metres above the astronomical tide, which could inundate low-lying areas of south coastal Andhra Pradesh.Heavy rainfall has already lashed parts of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, while Odisha has stepped up preparedness amid concerns over fresh damage following Cyclone Arnab.The IMD has warned that a storm surge of 1-1.5 metres above the astronomical tide could inundate low-lying areas of south coastal Andhra Pradesh until the morning of November 3. Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam districts are likely to experience the maximum surge before it gradually decreases.Heavy spells of rainfall are also expected along the south Andhra coast over the next 12 hours.Gale winds of 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph, are likely to continue along and off the coast until morning, the weather department said.Andhra Pradesh government rolled out a dedicated grievance reporting mechanism to provide swift assistance to citizens affected by Cyclone Murasu.Residents in cyclone-hit regions can report emergencies and civic disruptions—such as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situations—by sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009.The facility is designed to establish direct communication between citizens and administration, enabling prompt on-ground intervention and effective coordination during disaster management operations.According to officials, citizens can report cyclone-related grievances by following a simple step-by-step process: Send a "Hi" to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the "Services" option from the menu. Choose "Murasu Cyclone Issues". Click on "Report Issue" and confirm.Select "Registration" and enter essential details, including name, district, and mandal.At least 19 domestic flights were cancelled across Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam and Tirupati airports as the cyclone approached the Andhra Pradesh coast.Vijayawada Airport director M Lakshmi Kantha Reddy said IndiGo cancelled 10 flights and Air India Express two. Four flights were cancelled at Visakhapatnam airport, while three were cancelled at Tirupati airport.Chennai airport authorities also cancelled some flights and advised passengers to contact their respective airlines for updates.Chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to remain on alert as moderate to heavy rainfall and strong winds were expected across south coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema.Naidu expressed hope that the impact would be limited, citing forecasts of lower wind speeds and rainfall intensity compared with Cyclone Arnab.The state energy department also placed power utilities on high alert, directing officials to take precautionary measures to minimise damage to electricity infrastructure and ensure uninterrupted power supply.Energy minister G Ravi Kumar asked distribution companies to remain particularly vigilant in the vulnerable regions.Tamil Nadu extended assistance to its neighbouring state, deploying three National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams comprising 90 personnel and 25 electricity department teams with 500 personnel and essential equipment.Karnataka also announced that it would send 500 skilled power personnel along with equipment to help restore electricity infrastructure damaged by Cyclone Arnab.Heavy rainfall also lashed several parts of Chennai, Chengalpattu and Tiruvallur districts, with showers continuing since Sunday night.The weather department warned of very heavy rainfall in Chennai and Tiruvallur, while heavy showers were forecast for Chengalpattu, Kanchipuram, Ranipet, Vellore and the Nilgiris.Schools in Chennai were closed on Monday as authorities braced for further rainfall. The IMD said rain intensity was likely to ease only after the cyclone completely crossed the coast.Odisha stepped up evacuation efforts in vulnerable areas as the cyclone was expected to bring heavy rainfall to its southern districts, including Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri.Disaster management minister Suresh Pujari said district collectors had been alerted and more than 300 rescue teams from the NDRF, Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) and fire services had been kept on standby.Schools and colleges in some southern districts have been closed until November 3.The fresh weather threat has also raised concerns over the ongoing search for 10 people missing in a landslide.The approaching cyclone has added to the concerns of farmers whose standing crops were damaged by Cyclone Arnab and subsequent flooding.Ganjam district reported the maximum damage to paddy crops, with several fields inundated. Farmers fear another spell of heavy rainfall could cause further losses and damage crops nearing harvest.Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P Patil said Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent floods had affected 1.18 lakh people, damaged 1,672 houses and impacted 75,388 hectares of agricultural land.The agriculture department, however, estimated the damaged crop area at around 90,000 hectares.Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi announced a special relief package for those affected by Cyclone Arnab, adding that it would be reviewed after an assessment of the damage caused by Murasu.
Article Summary: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu made landfall along the south Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole early Tuesday. At least 19 domestic flights were cancelled across Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam and Tirupati airports. The IMD has warned that a storm surge of 1-1.5 metres above the astronomical tide could inundate low-lying areas.

Article Title: 'Don't travel by air. Next case': SC judge on plea alleging 700% airfare hike
Article Text:
The court did not take up the plea at that stage and proceeded to the next matter.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday responded sharply to a plea highlighting a steep surge in airfares, with Justice Vikram Nath telling the counsel, “Don’t travel by air. Next case,” before moving on to the next matter.The remark came after the counsel mentioned the plea before the court, claiming that airfares had increased by as much as 700 per cent. Arguing that air travel was an essential service, the counsel said the steep rise in ticket prices amounted to a violation of Article 14 of the Constitution, which guarantees equality before the law.“The airfares have increased to 700%. It is an essential service. Violation of Article 14,” the counsel submitted, according to Live Law.Justice Nath responded, “Don’t travel by air. Next case.”The court did not take up the plea at that stage and proceeded to the next matter. No order was passed on the submission.Meanwhile, India has adopted new airfare rules where government will not interfere in the process except “in an extraordinary situation (where) it considers it necessary to do so in the public interest.” Notified under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026, which will be applicable from Jan 1, 2027, government has continued its policy of letting market forces determine airfares without government interference.TOI reported on Oct 17 that India has no plans to regulate or cap airfares in the free market under which airlines here operate under the new airfare policy being finalised. However, it will keep a “strong lever” on airlines to ensure they don’t resort to very sharp surges in “exceptional and extraordinary circumstances” that see demand rising for certain routes.
Article Summary: Supreme Court responds sharply to a plea highlighting a steep surge in airfares. Justice Vikram Nath tells the counsel, “Don’t travel by air. Next case,” before moving on to the next matter. India has adopted new airfare rules where government will not interfere.

Article Title: Imran Khan tenders unconditional apology in HC over anti-SIR protest participation
Article Text:

Poll Vote & Share your view Should non-citizens be allowed to participate in protests in India? Yes, they should have a voice No, it's not their country Only in certain cases Unsure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Actor Imran Khan on Monday tendered an unconditional apology after the Bombay high court reprimanded him for participating in a protest against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls despite being a US citizen.A bench led by Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra questioned how the United States would have reacted if an Indian national had protested there."What for were you there? There's a complete difference between the rights of citizens and OCI card holders... You need to clarify whether you were there for protests or for some other work. You will have to categorically make a statement that you had no association with the protests, etc. Because the agitation was with regard to SIR, with which you have no concern at all," the court said."Obviously, because you aren't an Indian citizen... Imagine if an Indian citizen does such protests in any other country, take, for example, your country - the US. That Indian citizen would have been sent back to the country on the next immediate flight," the court added.Following Khan's apology, the Bombay high court scheduled the next hearing for December 7 and kept the "Leave India" notice against him in abeyance until then.The Bombay high court was hearing Khan's plea challenging a Leave India Notice (LIN) issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO), directing him to leave India by October 28. The court had earlier kept the notice in abeyance until November 2 and has now extended the relief until December 7.Khan, a US citizen and Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder, was issued the notice on October 14, days after he was detained during a protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in Mumbai on October 10.Following his detention, BJP leader Kirit Somaiya filed a police complaint alleging that Khan had violated OCI rules and visa conditions. The Mumbai Police subsequently forwarded an "unproven" FIR to the FRRO, which then issued the Leave India Notice.
Article Summary: Imran Khan tendered an unconditional apology after the Bombay high court reprimanded him for participating in a protest against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Khan, a US citizen and Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder, was issued the notice on October 14, days after he was detained during a protest.

NEW DELHI: Around 2.5 lakh shops across 20 to 25 major markets in Delhi remained closed on Sunday, with traders claiming losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore due to disruptions caused by the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season.Chamber of Trade & Industry (CTI) chairman Brijesh Goyal said nearly 80% of the approximately three lakh shops in markets surrounding the rally venue remained shut amid concerns over traffic restrictions, congestion and the expected arrival of large crowds.The disruption also affected the movement of customers, suppliers and dealers from towns surrounding the national capital. According to Goyal, around three lakh to four lakh people who regularly travel to Delhi for business did not arrive, while approximately 5,000 vehicles, including tempos and trucks, could not transport goods to markets in Old Delhi and Central Delhi.“Due to the rally held at Ramlila Maidan today, about 20 to 25 major markets in the vicinity were affected. These historic markets house approximately 3,00,000 shops. Based on data we received this evening from various WhatsApp groups—comprising traders from different markets under the CTA (Confederation of All India Traders)—about 80% of these shops—roughly 2,50,000 out of 3,00,000—remained closed today,” he said.Goyal added that loading and unloading operations were disrupted, affecting wholesale and retail businesses during one of the busiest periods of the year.“The movement of goods—loading and unloading—was completely disrupted. During the peak Diwali season, these markets with individual turnovers collectively generate business worth approximately 10,000 to 12,000 crore rupees. Even where shops remained open, sales were virtually non-existent; there were simply no customers,” he said.Putting the estimated losses at Rs 10,000-11,000 crore, Goyal questioned who would compensate traders for the business disruption.“The question now arises: who will compensate for this loss, or who will make up for it—will the organisers do so?” he said.He said the timing of the rally had compounded the impact, as traders were preparing for the festive rush ahead of Dhanteras, scheduled four days later. Businesses in the affected markets depend heavily on the movement of customers and goods during this period.Ahead of the gathering, traders across several major commercial hubs in Delhi had opposed holding the rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season. They warned that traffic congestion and restrictions could disrupt wholesale markets and affect the livelihoods of thousands of daily-wage workers.The Automotive Parts Merchant Association (APMA), based at Kashmere Gate, said the rally's location could affect commercial activity across a three-kilometre radius, covering several major trading hubs in the capital.APMA president Vinay Narang said traders were not opposed to democratic protests but objected to the timing and choice of venue."We are not aligned with any political party, nor are we against democratic protests. But the timing and the venue are completely wrong. Ramlila Maidan is located in the middle of Asia’s largest commercial zone—with major markets like Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazaar, Daryaganj, Mori Gate, and Kashmere Gate within a three-kilometre radius," Narang said.Amid concerns raised by traders' associations, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had appealed to people travelling to Delhi for the rally to support local businesses by shopping from their stores during the festive season.In a video message posted on X on Saturday, Gandhi urged participants to combine their participation in the protest with shopping from small businesses.“Tomorrow, lakhs of people are coming to Delhi for the Ramlila March. It is the festive season. The time of Diwali, Chhath, and Bhai Dooj has arrived. I want those lakhs of people coming to Delhi from outside to support the traders here,” Gandhi said.“Protest, march, hold rallies, and along with that, do a little shopping too - it will benefit the traders,” he added.The leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha also accused the BJP of spreading rumours about the rally's potential economic impact.“I know the rally will not harm the traders. The BJP is scared, that's why it's spreading rumours,” he said, adding, “But let's do both. Tomorrow there will be a march, there will be a rally, and lakhs of people will buy goods from the small shops of our traders.”The INDIA bloc held the rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging irregularities in the exercise.Several Opposition leaders attended the gathering, including Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Protesters also raised slogans such as "Vote chor, gaddi chhod", demanding accountability over alleged electoral irregularities.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Monday rejected claims that the INDIA bloc rally disrupted business in Delhi, alleging that the BJP's campaign warning of economic losses had been contradicted by increased shopping in local markets.In a post on X, Ramesh accused the BJP of spreading fear among traders and discouraging people from travelling to the national capital ahead of the rally. He said people arriving from different parts of the country were also expected to shop, benefiting businesses across Delhi."Every business operating in Delhi would benefit, directly or indirectly," he said.Ramesh alleged that the campaign was aimed at diverting attention from the Opposition's allegations of "vote theft" and protecting Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar."But the exact opposite happened," he said.Claiming that Rahul Gandhi's appeal had received a positive response, Ramesh said wholesale markets in Old Delhi had opened and business had picked up, while small shopkeepers and street vendors had also benefited."The people of Delhi and those who came from across the country responded to this smear campaign in their own way. In response to Rahul Gandhi ji's appeal, people went shopping in Delhi's markets. Shops in the wholesale markets of Old Delhi opened, and business boomed. On top of that, people bought goods in abundance from small shopkeepers and street vendors too. Newspaper reports themselves are exposing the falsehood of this fake narrative," he said.Thanking traders, shopkeepers and Delhi residents, Ramesh said they had supported local businesses alongside the democratic protest."The BJP should understand that the voice of democracy cannot be suppressed by fear or smear campaigns," he said.His remarks came in contrast to the estimates shared by CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal, who claimed that traders had suffered losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore, with around 2.5 lakh shops remaining closed.Earlier, Union Home Minister Amit Shah had criticised the Opposition over holding the rally during the festive shopping season, saying traders had repeatedly requested a postponement until after Diwali."Traders in Delhi pleaded with them, explaining that they have only one week in the entire year when the bulk of their business takes place. 'If we stock up on sweets and they don't sell, what happens? We suffer a loss. If we stock up on firecrackers and they don't sell, what happens? We suffer a loss...'" Shah said."The traders held press conferences--not once, but three times--wrote letters, and implored them to hold their rally after Diwali. But no—they insisted on holding their rally on that very day—the same dark day when the anti-Sikh riots, the Sikh massacre, took place," the Home Minister remarked.Before the rally, Rahul Gandhi had also accused the BJP of forcibly shutting shops in Delhi's Connaught Place and causing financial losses to local traders.In a post on X, Gandhi claimed that people attending the rally had been encouraged to support local businesses but found commercial establishments closed upon reaching the markets.
Article Summary: Traders claim Rs 10,000 crore loss as 2.5 lakh shops shut during INDIA bloc rally. Traders had warned of business losses ahead of rally. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had appealed to people travelling to Delhi for the rally to support local businesses by shopping from stores during the festive season.

Article Title: Nita Ambani marks birthday with foundation stone ceremony for 5,000-person care facility
Article Text: Nita Ambani marked her birthday on Sunday by laying the foundation stone for a proposed 100-acre care township in Karjat, Maharashtra. The project, Nita Mukesh Ambani Anant Ashray, is envisioned as a lifelong home for more than 5,000 people, including orphaned children, senior citizens and people with developmental disabilities.Mukesh Ambani and members of the Ambani family attended the bhumi pujan and groundbreaking ceremony near Mumbai. The township, being established by Reliance Foundation, will be developed as a permanent, not-for-profit institution in phases. It is planned as a community with residential homes, healthcare facilities, schools, rehabilitation services and opportunities for education, work and recreation.Nita Ambani said the project was a step towards creating “a loving home for people with disabilities, children who need a home and seniors who seek care and comfort”. She said the township would combine medical support with the warmth of family life and give residents opportunities to learn, work, make friends and participate in festivals and celebrations.According to the plans shared by Reliance Foundation, the township will support a wider community of approximately 15,000 people, including residents, caregivers, medical professionals, support staff and their families.The proposed facility will comprise eight residential villages, each named after a sacred river of India. Residents will live in small, family-style homes supported by house parents and caregivers. Their rooms will be designed to offer familiarity and personal belonging, with residents encouraged to personalise their living spaces.The project will include a specialised hospital offering developmental medicine, epilepsy care, special-needs dentistry, palliative care and other medical services. Rehabilitation facilities for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and hydrotherapy are also planned.Other proposed amenities include a temple, gardens, farms, playgrounds, workshops, cafés and inclusive sports and recreational facilities. An animal companionship farm is expected to be developed with expertise from Vantara.The township will also offer vocational training and employment opportunities through facilities such as a bakery, café and craft studios. A dedicated training academy for disability-care professionals, a hospice wing and a garden of remembrance are also part of the plans.The initiative is expected to have an impact beyond the township. Around 1,000 people from nearby areas are expected to access therapy, education and employment opportunities, while respite-care facilities, mobile medical clinics and outreach programmes will support families in neighbouring districts.
Article Summary: Mukesh Ambani and members of the Ambani family attended the bhumi pujan and groundbreaking ceremony near Mumbai. The township will be developed as a permanent, not-for-profit institution in phases. It is planned as a community with residential homes, healthcare facilities, schools, rehabilitation services and opportunities for education, work and recreation.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said no protest group can occupy a designated demonstration site indefinitely, observing that the right to protest must be balanced with the rights of other citizens. Hearing pleas filed by traders' associations over the impact of demonstrations in Delhi, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said designated protest venues must be made available to different groups for specific periods."You can't occupy a site for all times. Where farmers, journalists, etc. will go? Everyone has right to protest. Designated time must be given for designated period," CJI Surya Kant said, according to LiveLaw.The bench also said that orders granting permission for protests must clearly specify the reasons for allowing or refusing them. "You can't prevent other people, that I am doing protest now you can't," the CJI observed.The court was hearing pleas raising concerns over alleged police brutality, mass detentions, the closure of Metro stations and internet shutdowns during protests, besides the impact of demonstrations on businesses.A traders' counsel told the court that around 50 lakh people lived in areas surrounding the protest site and claimed that shops remained shut, with virtually nobody visiting Connaught Place. The court issued notices to the Centre and other authorities on a plea by the Kirana Committee Delhi seeking a halt to protests during the festive season.However, the bench said it could not adjudicate the traders' grievances unless all organisations involved in the protests were made parties to the proceedings. It asked the traders' associations to implead the organisers of the anti-CEC protests.The hearing comes weeks after the Centre de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, identifying Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as alternative venues for demonstrations.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said designated protest venues must be made available to different groups for specific periods. The bench also said that orders granting permission for protests must clearly specify the reasons for allowing or refusing them. The court issued notices to the Centre and other authorities on a plea by the Kirana Committee Delhi seeking a halt to protests.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday flagged the alleged open sale of conventional and uncertified firecrackers in Delhi markets despite its recent order allowing only certified green crackers ahead of Diwali.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale referred to a media report published on Tuesday, which highlighted the availability of different varieties of firecrackers in several markets across the national capital, according to Bar and Bench.The bench asked Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati to look into the alleged violations."In today's report, there's a photograph, they say that notwithstanding yesterday's order, now everything is available in the (firecracker) shops. Please look into it," Justice Sundresh told Bhati.The judge also referred to the report's claims that licensed and unlicensed crackers, including those with and without QR codes, were being sold openly."They say that in the market every other cracker, licensed, unlicensed, QR code, or no QR code, everything is available. Please take a note of it," he said.Also read: SC on Diwali: Crackers on Nov 7-8 in 2 time slots, and keep it green On November 2, the Supreme Court allowed the sale of certified green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR from November 4 to 6 and their use on November 7 and 8, subject to restrictions.Firecrackers can be burst only between 6am and 7am and 8pm and 10pm on these two days. A complete ban will be restored from November 9.The court had clarified that only firecrackers certified by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) and the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO) could be manufactured and sold.It also restricted sales to designated locations and prohibited online sales. Each box must carry a product-specific QR code to verify its certification. The manufacture of firecracker strings, or laris, and crackers containing barium was also prohibited.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday flagged the alleged open sale of conventional and uncertified firecrackers in Delhi markets. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale referred to a media report published on Tuesday. Article Title: NHAI to use desilted river material for road projects in Bihar, says transport minister Gadkari
Article Text:
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has embarked on an innovative project to leverage materials from Bihar's rivers for highway development

The national highways authority of India (NHAI) will use sand and other materials excavated from rivers and water bodies in Bihar for highway construction, union road transport minister Nitin Gadkari said after the Bihar government and the road transport ministry signed an MoU.Nitin Gadkari said the initiative would also help mitigate flooding in the state.The Bihar chief minister said the state faces floods not only due to its own water but also because of water flowing in from other regions, including Nepal. He noted that the highest flood levels (HFL) had risen in three rivers despite Bihar receiving less rainfall this year.Desilting rivers and water bodies could help reduce the impact of floods, the chief minister said, adding that desilting the Ganga and reclaiming land along its banks could create space for one lakh Ganga-facing homes.
Article Summary: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) will use sand and other materials excavated from rivers and water bodies in Bihar for highway construction. Article Title: Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response on whereabouts of Barman from Bangladesh
Article Text:
Barman came on medical visa for treatment at Siliguri in West Bengal on March 20 last year, attended the hospital for two days, then went to Thakur Anukul Chandra Ashram at Deoghar and is untraceable since March 24 last year.

NEW DELHI: Bipul Chandra Barman, a resident of ‘Hindu Prodhan Para’ in Panchagarh district of Bangladesh, came on medical visa for treatment at Siliguri in West Bengal on March 20 last year, attended the hospital for two days, then went to Thakur Anukul Chandra Ashram at Deoghar and is untraceable since March 24 last year.For the ministry of external affairs (MEA), additional solicitor general Archana Pathak Dave informed the Supreme Court, which has in session of a habeas corpus petition by Barman’s wife in session, that the person remains untraceable and that the relatives must lodge a zero FIR relating to a missing person complaint with Jharkhand police at Deoghar.The wife, through her counsel, said on Jun 30 last year, the Bangladesh High Commission in Kolkata, acting on a request from MEA, issued a letter to the Bangladesh government seeking verification of a person detained in India and identified as Bipul Chandra Pradhan. In August last year, the Bangladesh foreign ministry sent a letter to the Indian home ministry confirming that Barman is a Bangladeshi citizen and has no criminal antecedents.In search of her husband, the wife travelled to India and gave representation for Barman’s release in June this year. Finding no response, she moved the SC.What was intriguing for the SC was the categorical denial by the MEA that Barman has neither been detained, arrested, nor deported by Indian authorities and that his status remains as a missing person.Dave also informed the court that Indian authorities have not communicated at all with the Bangladesh counterparts on Barman.Adding further complications to an already complicated case, the West Bengal government informed the court that Barman’s mobile phone number was found to be used by a person at Barh in Bihar, which is proximate to Deoghar in Jharkhand, the place he visited last before becoming untraceable.The CDR analysis showed his last known location was at a temple in Matigara, a place near Siliguri.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the ASG, who informed the Bangladesh Deputy High Commissioner about the detention of Barman and sought verification of his citizenship and antecedents. SC directed the Union government to file a detailed status report after examining all the leads given in the petition and the status report filed by the West Bengal government.
Article Summary: Bipul Chandra Barman, a resident of ‘Hindu Prodhan Para’ in Panchagarh district of Bangladesh, came on medical visa for treatment at Siliguri in West Bengal on March 20 last year. Article Title: E-sign for SIR tribunal judges soon, can upload bulk orders on portal
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Having updated the appellate tribunal portal for West Bengal around two weeks back to enable judges to rely on documents beyond the 13 listed in SIR order, the Election Commission (EC) will, within this week, also replace Aadhaar-authenticated e-sign with digital signature certificate (DSC), as a mandatory requirement for the judges to login and upload their orders.According to sources in the commission, two more requests from SIR tribunal judges have been accepted and operationalised. The appellate tribunals platform now enable the judges to upload their orders in bulk, rather than one at a time. This is expected to save effort and time, given that a large number of orders passed by the tribunals in over a month were not uploaded due to the judges’ reservations about the Aadhaar authentication screen introduced in September this year.The ECINET portal would also allow judges to save their orders as drafts, enabling them to make changes before issuing the final order.Sources told TOI that the commission had, nearly two weeks back, tweaked its dedicated portal for the tribunals, adding a 14th category to the list of eligible documents, namely “any other document”. This now allows the judges’ office to upload a document that the judge, based on his discretion, deems apt to determine a person’s eligibility to be included in the electoral roll; even the electoral registration officer or the elector can upload this document on the portal, as per sources.All SIR orders issued by EC thus far specifically state that the list of 13 documents is “only indicative (not exhaustive)”.“The DSC-based access for the tribunal judges is likely to be cleared before the end of this week, with the pen-drive containing the digital signatures under process,” shared an EC officer.TOI has further learnt that EC has already instructed the West Bengal chief electoral officer (CEO) to work on the tribunal judges’ demand for relocation of their offices to a more “convenient and central” location. “It is a work in progress and alternative locations are being explored in consultation with the judges,” said a commission official.The tribunals are hearing nearly lakhs of appeals against orders passed by Calcutta High Court–appointed judicial officers in West Bengal regarding inclusions and exclusions from the electoral roll.update the aboe onefile this one-Bharti Jain/TNNNew Delhi: The Centre has notified three new foreigners regional registration offices (FRROs) — in Bhubaneswar, Kohima, Agartala, taking the total number of such offices to 20 in the country.Stating that the number of foreign visitors arriving for tourism, medical and educational purposes has witnessed a substantial rise, the home ministry in a statement said there is need to appoint FRROs in each state. “This will ensure service accessibility, enhance regulatory compliance and promote India as an attractive destination,” it said while reiterating home minister Amit Shah’s call for establishing FRROs in all state capitals by 2027.The FRRO monitors compliance with Indian immigration laws, handles cases of overstay and visa violations, and coordinates legal action or penalties where necessary.In the past couple of years, five new FRROs have become operational in Jaipur, Chandigarh, Aizawl (Mizoram), Amravati (Andhra Pradesh) and Guwahati.“Recently, three new FRRO offices, namely Kohima (Nagaland), Agartala (Tripura) and Bhubaneshwar (Odisha), have been notified. Earlier, Kohima and Agartala were under the jurisdiction of FRRO, Kolkata, whereas Bhubaneshwar was under the jurisdiction of FRRO, Hyderabad,” shared the MHA.The government is considering further increasing the FRRO network in the remaining states, namely Bihar, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Meghalaya.The 20 FRROs across the country are located at Ahmedabad, Amravati, Amritsar, Aizawl, Agartala, Bengaluru, Bhubaneswar, Calicut, Chennai, Cochin, Chandigarh, Delhi, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Kohima, Kozhikode, Lucknow, Mumbai and Trivandrum," the statement read.The expansion of the FRRO office network has a dual focus on facilitating foreigners' legitimate travel and stay in India and ensuring effective implementation of immigration laws and security requirements.
Article Summary: EC eases SIR tribunal procedures in Bengal, allowing bulk order uploads, draft saving and additional documents, while planning digital signature-based login for judges. Centre has notified three new foreigners regional registration offices (FRROs) — in Bhubaneswar, Kohima, Agartala, taking the total number of such offices to 20.

Article Title: Investment in renewable energy cushioned Iran war blow: PM Modi
Article Text:
PM Modi says clean energy investments cushioned India against West Asia crisis, sets 500GW target by 2030

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi said India's economic growth has remained high despite the West Asia crisis, whose impact would have been far more serious if the country had not invested in clean energy over the past decade.Commending India's progress in renewable energy sector, he said efforts were on to add 500GW of non-fossil energy capacity over the next 10-11 years. The PM also pitched for a "clean cooking movement" to reduce dependence on imported gas.Speaking at the inauguration of Bharat Renewable Energy Summit at Bharat Mandapam Monday, Modi said the ongoing energy crisis had underlined the link between energy security and economic security, making it imperative for countries to reduce dependence on fossil fuels."This global crisis has given every country a clear message that energy security is directly linked to economic security. If we continue to remain too dependent on fossil fuels, global economy will continue to be disrupted again and again," he said.Modi said India had already achieved nearly 300GW of non-fossil installed power capacity, accounting for more than 50% of its total capacity, and was pursuing its target of 500GW capacity by 2030.India's clean energy sector could offer investment opportunities exceeding Rs 20 lakh crore ($220 billion) by the end of the decade as the country expands renewable energy generation, transmission infrastructure, manufacturing and energy storage. More than Rs 15 lakh crore ($164 billion) had been invested in the sector over the past decade, including Rs 6 lakh crore ($63 billion) in the last two years."For all of you, a new sky of opportunities is about to open up in India's clean energy sector," he said, adding it was difficult to find "political and policy stability" like India's anywhere in the world.Referring to schemes such as PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana and PM-Kusum, Modi said India was making solar power part of citizens' lives. He called on farmers to move beyond solar pumps and become energy producers by installing panels on vacant farmland and along field boundaries. "Annadata should become Urjadata," he said.In a push to reduce dependence on imported cooking gas, Modi urged startups and innovators to develop solutions that would enable households to use rooftop solar power for cooking. He also pitched for wider adoption of electric vehicles, with households charging them using solar power generated on their rooftops.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi says clean energy investments cushioned India against West Asia crisis, sets 500GW target by 2030. He said efforts were on to add 500GW of non- fossil energy capacity over the next 10-11 years. The PM also pitched for a "clean cooking movement" to reduce dependence on imported gas.

Article Title: Cyclone Murasu to make landfall near at Andhra coast tonight; 120 kmph winds expected
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Cyclone Murasu, which has intensified into a Severe Cyclonic Storm, is expected to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur in the early hours of Tuesday, bringing winds of up to 120 kmph, extremely heavy rainfall and the threat of coastal flooding. The cyclone is forecast to make landfall south of Ongole between 11:30 pm on Monday and 4 am on Tuesday.According to the India Meteorological Department ( IMD ), Murasu intensified into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the west-central and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal in the early hours of Monday. In its Press Release issued on November 2, IMD said Cyclone Murasu was centred at 14.1°N latitude and 81.4°E longitude at 8:30 am on Monday, around 160 km east-southeast of Nellore and 180 km northeast of Chennai.The IMD has warned of strong winds and heavy rainfall across several districts of Andhra Pradesh, including Krishna, Bapatla, Prakasam, Nellore, Guntur, Eluru, NTR, Palnadu and West Godavari.Chennai, Thiruvallur, Ranipet, Kancheepuram and Chengalpattu in north Tamil Nadu, along with parts of Puducherry, are also expected to experience strong winds and rainfall. Southern Odisha districts, including Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri, are also under warning.Telangana and Rayalaseema are likely to receive heavy to extremely heavy rainfall.Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has reviewed cyclone preparedness and directed officials to coordinate rescue and relief operations. Six NDRF and seven SDRF teams have been deployed, while control rooms and evacuation arrangements have been put in place.The IMD has advised a complete suspension of fishing operations along the affected coastal areas. Fishermen have been warned against venturing into the west-central Bay of Bengal until the afternoon of November 4 and along the Andhra Pradesh coast during the same period. The weather agency has also cautioned against the movement of motorboats and small ships due to dangerous sea conditions.Murasu is expected to weaken into a cyclonic storm by Tuesday morning, with wind speeds reducing to 70–80 kmph, gusting to 90 kmph.
Article Summary: Cyclone Murasu is expected to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur in the early hours of Tuesday. The cyclone is forecast to make landfall south of Ongole between 11:30 pm on Monday and 4 am on Tuesday.

NEW DELHI: The Centre has notified grievance redressal rules under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), or VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, laying down a multi-tier mechanism to address complaints related to the implementation of the rural employment scheme.Under the new rules, grievances will have to be resolved within 15 days of receipt, while the enquiry into each complaint must be completed within seven working days. The framework provides for grievance redressal officers at the Gram Panchayat, block and district levels, with the District Programme Coordinator overseeing the process at the district level.The rules allow people to submit complaints in person, through speed post, designated digital platforms, telephone helplines or other channels specified by state governments. Complaints received physically at the panchayat, block or district level must be registered on the designated digital platform on the day of receipt or, if that is not feasible, by the next working day.Once registered, complainants will receive an acknowledgement with a registration number, date of receipt and details of the receiving authority. The rules also state that “no grievance can be refused registration” on the grounds of its format, language, mode of submission or procedural deficiencies.The designated officer will examine each complaint and can seek relevant records, documents and information from the authorities concerned. Complainants may also be given an opportunity to present their case, either in person or electronically, before the grievance is disposed of.The findings and action taken will be recorded on the designated digital platform and communicated to the complainant. Complaints that remain unresolved within the 15-day deadline will be escalated to the next higher level under the state grievance redressal mechanism and monitored until disposal.The rules also provide for appeals against orders passed under the grievance redressal mechanism, in accordance with Schedule I of the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025.
Article Summary: The Centre has notified grievance redressal rules under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), or VB-G RAM G Act, 2025. The rules lay down a multi-tier mechanism to address complaints related to the implementation of the rural employment scheme.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites
